links.reason: Both say deeds' hold is loosened (தீவினைப் பசை பறந்தன vs இருள்சேர் இருவினையும் சேரா), but the epic line ends பலர்க்கு மென்பவே, a report of portents at a birth, not a doctrine of release. The 'gains' put a condition (devotee's praise) into the epic verse that the verse never states.

The epic image is the earth as a woman who leaves each king (பேர்ந்திலள்); the Siddhar has no earth-woman, only kings burnt to a fistful of ash that becomes earth (பிடிசாம்பராய் வெந்து மண்ணாவது). They share the theme of royal impermanence, not a reversed image, and the Siddhar gains no living figure from 2088.

271 says the ascetic thinks only 'each one's own deed' (தத்தம்வினை), and Naladiyar 58 says the worthy grieve for scorners who will fall to hell; both read pain through karma but the pairing is theme. Nothing in 271 concerns a king with dogs, so the Naladiyar 'gain' is invented, and 'omits pity' is an argument from silence.

1052 is only a friend reporting a drum for tomorrow's wedding (முரசெறி இமிழிசை), with no hint of loss; Naladiyar 23 turns on wedding drums becoming பிணப்பறை. The link is the shared word 'drum', and the note itself says the epic verse lacks the thought. The sense of 1052 is also flagged uncertain.

Both verses use the nectar-and-poison image (இன் அமிர்தும் நஞ்சும் in 250, நஞ்சுணின் அமுதமாகும் in 2314), one of the king's fire, the other of deeds. The link is real, but the two do not make incompatible claims about one thing; the shift from king to karma is a change of speaker's argument, so same_image or develops fits better than tension.

2017 says those with காட்சி lit, even வதமிலர், reach the world of gods or பேரின்ப வெள்ளம்; Kural 356 says those who learn and see the true thing go to the path of no return. Kural 356 says nothing of vows, so the claim that the couplet 'gains' that vows are not required is an imposition, and the verse's two destinations are left open (sense flagged).

links.reason: 325 likens the merchant's leaving the dead son to ascetics leaving the body for a golden one (பொன் உடம்பு அடைந்தது ஒப்பவே); Kural 338 compares body and life to a bird leaving a குடம்பை. The couplet's figure is detachment, not 'loss', so the contrast is overstated, and the 'abandoned nest without penance' gain is not in the epic.

Both are sermons to Payapati; 2018 says the lamp of காட்சி destroys the dark of deeds, 2072 adds ஞானம், purity of mind and long meditation before release. That adds conditions rather than extends a first step, since 2018 does not call the lamp a first step; it fits qualifies, and the link is sound in direction but its teaches overstates 2018.

In 358 Sumantiri says ஊழது விளைவு and a plan pressed hard may end otherwise (கருதிற்றின்றி மற்றோராறாக நண்ணும்), then still offers to speak more (இனிச் சிறிது உரைப்பன்). That is the couplet's claim (சூழினும் தான் முந்துறும்) used as a counsellor's caution, and the note states both ends correctly.

202 gives release as a form and bliss kept (சுடரொளி உருவம் தாங்கி ... இன்பம்), while Tirumanthiram 136 says the soul is contained in Sivam as salt in water (சீவன் சிவத்துள் அடங்குமே). The conflict depends on reading அடங்கும் as loss of being, which the marker itself says is unsettled; the 'gains' rest on silence (no one named to join).

1287 is snake-bite lore sorting snakes by smell into அந்தணன், அரசன், வணிகன், சூத்திரன்; Kural 972 says birth is alike for all living beings and differences come from செய்தொழில். The verse makes no claim about people's birth-rank, so there is no incompatible claim; the pairing stretches 'all living beings' to snakes.

2070 describes the chain (birth, senses, desire and hatred, hidden deeds, return), and Kural 349 says births are cut at the moment attachment ends (பற்றற்ற கண்ணே பிறப்பறுக்கும்). But 2070 never shows the break; it describes the continuing return, so 'shown to be the point where the chain is broken' is not in the verse.

links.reason: 326 gives the fruit of killing (குருதியாறிடக் கொன்ற தீவினை ... அருநரகு) and 4 is a proem on deeds that come on and ripen, but 4 is flagged hard to parse and does not 'state in the abstract that a deed binds and ripens' clearly. A sermon applying the general doctrine of the poem's start is an illustration, and the later verse does not answer or reverse the earlier.

Both name bathing at Kumari with laughter, but 2020 has Civakan feign a wish to cure old age (முதுமூப்பொழிவு), while the Thiruppugazh poet fears being mocked as a diseased wretch. Two verses, five centuries apart, do not show that the Kumari pilgrim was a 'stock figure of ridicule'; the claim also leans on 2021, not in the packet.

2619 urges penance and giving before black hair turns white, and 2799 lists loss of youth and old age among sufferings (இளமை நீங்க மூப்புவந்து அடைதல் துன்பம்). The sermon states the same topic of youth lapsing, but the pairing is theme; the speaker of 2619 is itself uncertain, and 'her urging reads as the doctrine put plainly' is not shown.

157 has the father crown his son and then take the ascetic form (மகுடஞ் சூட்டிப் போகம்விட்டு), an illustration of renunciation. Kural 342's 'in time' is supplied by commentary (the verse says வேண்டின் உண்டாகத் துறக்க), and 'installing the heir' is not what the couplet is about, so the 'gains' on the couplet side are imposed.

links.reason: Akananuru 44 has the war over and the man bidding the charioteer drive home (ஊர்க பாக ... இன்துயில் பெறவே); Kural 1268 says let the king win and let us feast at home. The shared pattern is real but 'the Kural reduces the akam formula' is a claim of derivation that the pair does not show, and the Kural's speaker is disputed.

Kural 586 has spies in the guise of ascetics; Purananuru 47 says the bard's life of gifts (பரிசில் வாழ்க்கை) is not known to harm others (பிறர்க்குத் தீதறிந்தன்றோ இன்றே). The poem never names suspicion of wandering poets and the bard is not a renunciant, so the 'tension' rests on a charge the marker inferred.

161 is only praise at the peak (மலிவு எய்தினான்) and contains no fall; the fall is told from the next verse. Naladiyar 3 (kings fall when deeds turn, enemies take wives) is not developed by this unit, and the epic queen is driven out, not taken by enemies as the quatrain says.

Naga Kumara 3 uses the bright lamp with smoke (புகைக்கொடி உள்ளுண்டென்றே ... விளக்கை இகழ்ச்சியின் நீப்பாரில்லை) and Cintamani 4 the unwashed gem (கழுவாது விட்டால்); these are two images, not a shared one. The shared element is the proem apology, a convention rather than an image, so same_image does not fit.

Soolamani 3 asks that the wise guard lapses (அற்றங்கள் காப்பார்) and Cintamani 4 that the learned wash out the flaw (மறுவும் மதியால் கழூஉவி); the contrast is real but small, and neither limits the other, so qualifies does not fit. This is a difference within a shared proem convention.

In 1196 the bowstring is named நாண், and the subject of உயிரினும் மதிக்கற்பாலது is not fixed by the clipped syntax; Kural 969 uses the yak's hair for mānam. The epic here illustrates honour above life with a pun; the 'gain' that the couplet gets the bowstring in place of the yak is a swap, not an addition.

Both have a mother going after an eloped girl and asking those on the road (Ak 7 a doe and a hill girl; Kalittokai 9 brahmin ascetics, 'காணிரோ'), so the shared figure is real. But the Kalittokai answer is a consolation by analogy (சாந்தம், முத்தம், யாழ்), not a 'debate the elopement wins', and 'later anthology' turning one into the other is not shown.

290 mourns the king as அறச் செங்கோல் and 261 shows him sunk in pleasure having given up his army; they are the same narrator seeing two causes, not an incompatible claim. A lament praises the dead and the earlier verse gives the opening for treachery; qualifies fits better than tension.

3070 has the sun's ring burn while he stands on the elephant of knowledge beside a gold post; there is no gold being fired, and no shining stated in the verse. Kural 267's image is gold that shines the more it burns, so the verse illustrates austerity without the couplet's image and the 'gains' are not in the Tamil.

Kural 55 says the wife who does not worship a god but rises worshipping her husband commands the rain; 221 has Vijayai offer to எம் பெருமான் அடி and then go to தம் பெருமான் அடி. The parallel lines give an order of two devotions that the couplet's flat 'not a god' does not allow, so the epic really qualifies it.

913 pairs அவாவெனும் கடல் and தவாவினை (the same two words as Kural 367) with giving to suppliants as damming the sea; the connection is two shared words, not a quoted run. The marker flags the sense uncertain, and the 'doctrinal source' gain assumes derivation from the couplet that the Tamil does not show.

46 has the sister saying there is no fear in leaving a fearful life (விடுவதற் கஞ்சலுண்டோ) and 62 has the youths unshaken (நடுக்கமின்றி நின்றாம்) when asked why they laugh. The later unit matches the earlier resolve, but the reason given in 62 is only that fear is useless (அஞ்சுதற் பயனின்றே), and 'garden of talk' and 'killing ground' are not in the verses.

Both verses give the Lord red feet (சேவடி, செம்மலர்த் திருந்தடி), but செம்மலரடி is a stock epithet of the Jina. 1903's question whether lotus petals redden the feet is a conceit of its own; no allusion to 181 is shown, so 'plays on the earlier praise' is unsupported.

916 reports the soldiers saying life is taken only by bound fate (ஒட்டிய வூழினன்றி உயிர்கொளல் ஒழிக); Kural 380 says nothing is stronger than fate. The link is a shared idea, and 'makes its arms servants of fate' is the marker's reading of a clipped verse; the 'gains' on the Kural side add a picture, not a qualification.

links.reason: In 223 Vijayai dreams the asoka tree fell utterly (தொலைந்து அற வீழ்ந்தது) with a shoot growing from its foot; in 267 Saccandan says the dream she dreamt has all come to pass (கனவு எல்லாம் விளைந்த). The later unit fulfils the earlier, and the note says which.

108 foretells a man coming with a letter into the garden Pushpakarandam (புட்பமா கரண்டமென்னும் பொழிலகத்து இழியும்); 430 only describes a grove of that name, with no messenger or date. The fulfilment is in 429, which this unit does not carry, so the verse alone shows the shared name and nothing answering the prophecy.

2563 hymns a stainless Jina with the wheel (மலமறு திகிரியை) and the master of the senses; 3023 has the sea of virtues (குணக்கடல்) and the wheel of dharma. The sea of virtues is not in 2563, so 'the same epithets recur' is only half true, and two hymns to the Jina do not 'develop'; this is repetition of a convention.

243 lists the fruits of the vows in the order not killing, truth, not stealing (கொலையின தின்மை ... வாய்மை ... களவின் மீட்சி), which is the standard vow order, not a ranking. Kural 323's point is a ranking (கொல்லாமை first, பொய்யாமை after), so 'the verse supplies a ranking the couplet has' is not shown; the sense is flagged uncertain.

211 argues that the blame of lust cannot be hidden (படு பழி மறைக்கல் ஆமோ), and Naladiyar 89 says lust burns the mind, worse than fire or sun. The shared topic is lust's harm; 'the epic chose reputation' is a guess about intent, and the quatrain gains nothing from the speech.

36 praises the lord of the vow of not killing (கொல்லாத நல்விரதக் கோமான்) and says worshippers cut the evil birth; Kural 321 states not killing as the whole of virtue. The verse illustrates the Kural's rule, and the 'gains' (the Kural makes a person of the rule; the verse gets a reason) add nothing that is in the Tamil.

Poem 14 lists the beloved's shoulders, eyes, teeth, hair and breasts (மணமௌவல் முகை அன்ன ... வெண்பல்) as praise now withdrawn, and 22 asks whether he praised the same teeth, hair and breasts when old (தளர்முலை பாராட்டினையோ). The shared blazon is real, but 22 does not extend 14; they are two poems of one poet on one device, so develops does not fit.

The death enacts the dream's first image and the shoot is the child still to come, so the later unit fulfils the earlier.

The note's 'order of dressing, mounting and rushing' belongs to Paripadal 12, so the claim that the epic keeps it, and a lineage of convention, is not in the verse.
